event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: PepsiCo’s 2023 filing presents COVID-19 chiefly as a still-unfolding, enterprise-wide risk that has already affected – and can continue to affect – demand patterns, supply-chain continuity, commodity costs and labour availability.  All mentions are post-event (March 2020) and therefore within the recent 0-3-year window, so the Time Decay Principle allows relatively high severity scores.  The disclosures concede that pandemics ‘have impacted’ results to date (showing realised exposure) and warn of on-going vulnerabilities, but they remain largely qualitative: no dollar figures, margin effects or probability assessments are supplied.  The language is specific enough to tie the pandemic to concrete operational areas (consumer demand, product availability, raw-material volatility, labour shortages), yet it also blends COVID-19 with other broad risk drivers and offers few detailed mitigants.  Accordingly, individual snippets merit mid-to-upper-range scores (5-7) rather than the maximum, reflecting clear, recent, multi-faceted impact acknowledgement without quantified materiality.

evidence_list.snippet: Pandemics, epidemics or other disease outbreaks, such as COVID-19, have also impacted and could continue to impact consumer preferences and demand for our products.

components.reason: States that pandemics ‘have impacted’ demand – confirms realised, not just potential, effect.
Specifically cites COVID-19, directly linking the risk to the global pandemic in scope.
Adds forward-looking clause ‘could continue’, extending the risk horizon.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides an explicit, recent connection between COVID-19 and actual as well as future demand erosion, but without quantification or mitigation, yielding a solid mid-high score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, our business operations, including our supply chain, are subject to disruption by natural disasters, pandemics, epidemics or other events beyond our control that could negatively impact product availability and decrease demand for our products if our crisis management plans do not effectively mitigate these issues.

components.reason: Highlights supply-chain disruption risk tied to pandemics.
Links disruption to negative product availability and demand – operational and revenue threats.
Notes absence of effective mitigation (‘if our crisis management plans do not effectively mitigate’).
No figures or probability estimates provided.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Demonstrates concrete operational exposure (supply-chain and product availability) with no quantified scale, producing a moderate-high risk score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: The raw materials and other supplies, including agricultural commodities, fuel and packaging materials, such as recycled PET, transportation, labor and other supply chain inputs that we use for the manufacturing, production and distribution of our products are subject to price volatility and fluctuations in availability caused by many factors, including ... health epidemics or pandemics or other contagious outbreaks (including COVID-19), labor shortages or changes in availability of our or our business partners’ workforce (including the lack of availability of truck drivers or as a result of COVID-19) ...

components.reason: Explicitly lists COVID-19 as a driver of raw-material price and availability volatility.
Describes multiple cascading effects (price volatility, labour shortages) – broad operational risk amplification.
Positions the risk as current and continuing but offers no numbers.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures wide-ranging cost and supply-chain exposure triggered by COVID-19, but remains qualitative, warranting a score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: As a global company with deep local ties, we faced many of the same challenges in 2022 as our consumers, customers, and competitors across the world, including supply chain disruptions; inflationary pressures; shifting consumer preferences and behaviors; another year of the COVID-19 pandemic; a worsening climate crisis; a highly competitive operating environment; a rapidly changing retail landscape, including the growth in e-commerce; continued macroeconomic and political volatility, including the deadly conflict in Ukraine; and an evolving regulatory landscape.

components.reason: Acknowledges ‘another year of the COVID-19 pandemic’ as an experienced 2022 challenge – confirms ongoing impact.
Places COVID-19 alongside supply-chain and demand-shift challenges, implying material operational influence.
Statements relate to the most recent fiscal year, maximising temporal relevance.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Links COVID-19 to 2022 performance with explicit acknowledgement of its role among key global headwinds, justifying a higher score of 7.
